review_method: Manual comparison of every non-null answer against every authored semantic requirement. Repeated development answers were still inspected as separate responses; a shared rationale is used only when the same rubric gap recurs.

partial_rationale_by_question.q001: The answer provides useful families but does not fully distinguish every authored family, task mapping, hybrid case, and benchmark role.
partial_rationale_by_question.q002: At least one required pipeline contrast remains incomplete; the recurring gaps are extraction alternatives and the accuracy, cost, updateability, and task-scope trade-off.
partial_rationale_by_question.q003: The graph-origin distinction is useful, but task overlap and the extraction-error/cost versus supplied-graph coverage/schema trade-off are not both fully addressed.
partial_rationale_by_question.q004: The retrieval-unit comparison is useful, but at least one required precision, pruning-cost, detail-loss, or hybrid multi-granular trade-off remains incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q005: Community construction and use are explained, but abstraction, redundancy, token cost, and local-detail loss are not all materially covered.
partial_rationale_by_question.q006: The answer compares paths, subgraphs, or graph queries, but does not fully cover verification/pruning and the fixed-versus-exploratory completeness/noise trade-off.
partial_rationale_by_question.q007: The diffusion and adaptive mechanisms are described, but the explicit optimization contrast and mechanism-to-task trade-offs are not fully developed.
partial_rationale_by_question.q009: Decomposition, planning, and routing are covered, but latency, token use, robustness, and execution validity are not all evaluated.
partial_rationale_by_question.q010: The response describes structured context, but does not fully compare every required organization unit and its fidelity, redundancy, abstraction, and token-budget constraints.
partial_rationale_by_question.q011: Hybrid retrieval is explained, but semantic-gap, disconnected-evidence, graph-noise, and cost trade-offs are not all addressed.
partial_rationale_by_question.q012: The LLM, graph, and classical-NLP division is useful, but extraction-error propagation, offline expense, online flexibility, and explainability are not all covered.
partial_rationale_by_question.q013: Offline costs and updates are discussed, but the construction-alternative contrast and downstream quality/domain-semantics trade-off remain incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q014: The response covers prompt size and pruning but omits part of the repeated-call, verification/reflection, bridge-evidence, and offline-versus-online cost analysis.
partial_rationale_by_question.q015: Static, incremental, and query-time adaptation are distinguished, but deduplication, mutual indexes, provenance, schema/community maintenance, and error accumulation are incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q016: Retrieval filtering is covered, but preventive deduplication/schema controls, generator distraction, and the risk of filtering bridge evidence are not all addressed.
partial_rationale_by_question.q017: Failure modes and mitigations are useful, but the schema-versus-adaptability trade-off and residual incompleteness limitation are not fully stated.
partial_rationale_by_question.q018: Auditability and noisy-graph risks are discussed, but medical/fact-checking examples and calibrated integration without equating evidence with correctness are incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q019: External-versus-parametric control is discussed, but freshness/domain specificity, irrelevant-evidence suppression, and the full risk/evidence-sufficiency balance are incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q020: Domain adaptations and reusable retrieval patterns are described, but risk controls, transfer cost, and benchmark or ontology mismatch are incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q022: The structural value of graphs is explained, but preprocessing cost, abstraction loss, iterative latency, and token efficiency are not all balanced.
partial_rationale_by_question.q024: The answer separates several evaluation axes but does not fully cover comprehensiveness/diversity, fair baselines, and all component-level comparisons.
partial_rationale_by_question.q025: The evaluation critique is useful, but leakage or unrelated-question effects and separate construction/retrieval/generation versus end-to-end evaluation are not always fully covered.
partial_rationale_by_question.q026: Inspectable paths are covered, but relation ordering, retriever traceability versus causal generator use, and noisy or plausible-but-unfaithful explanations remain incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q027: Community construction is well described, but global/filtering/fact-checking use and resolution, cross-community, and fine-detail limitations are incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q029: The static/adaptive contrast is useful, but concrete mechanisms and the complete latency, token, non-determinism, and error-propagation balance are incomplete.
partial_rationale_by_question.q030: The decision framework is strong but does not fully cover construction/reuse, every retrieval family, and the complete grounding, robustness, and efficiency evaluation set.
